decisionRule: Use WirePlumber default/target metadata for every one-to-one ordinary route; create raw links only for an explicitly planned advanced shape that metadata cannot express.

canonicalStages.subject: managed decoder capture stream
canonicalStages.target: selected TV or Bluetooth Audio/Source endpoint

canonicalStages.subject: managed CamillaDSP playback stream
canonicalStages.target: selected main-speaker or headset Audio/Sink endpoint

canonicalStages.subject: ordinary movable playback streams governed by follow-default policy
canonicalStages.target: selected main-speaker or headset Audio/Sink endpoint

advancedShapes.reason: One target.object value cannot route one stream concurrently to several independently verified outputs.
advancedShapes.processorRequirement: Use a declared fan-out/adapter processor when format, clock, latency, or channel contracts differ between branches.

advancedShapes.reason: Default and target metadata select destinations; they do not define gains or combine several sources into one signal.
advancedShapes.processorRequirement: A declared mixer processor owns mixing semantics; links only connect its planned inputs and output.

advancedShapes.reason: Use explicit links only when a prepared processor exposes fixed ports or channel-specific topology that WirePlumber target metadata cannot represent.
advancedShapes.processorRequirement: The processor plan must declare every internal link; topology is never inferred from the live graph.

evidence.claim: A real WirePlumber policy process routes an ordinary playback stream through configured default metadata and moves it through target.object without owned raw links.
Explicit links are uniquely owner-tagged, idempotent, and cannot adopt or remove unmanaged topology.
The released binding contract records the default/target versus managed-link boundary.
The existing editor represents user-facing graph intent; runtime mechanism remains a backend plan/explanation concern for the future orchestration UI.

pendingAcceptance: The released binding integration test proves ordinary playback default/target movement; capture-stream and complete decoder/CamillaDSP chain acceptance remains task 13.7.
Target Raspberry Pi timing and audio-gap behavior remain deferred hardware measurements and do not change this mechanism boundary.
